title: Practise it today, at work
caption: The skills you use with colleagues are the skills you use with AI, so you can practise them at work, today.

handoff.title: 01 · The handoff
handoff.work: Hand off work to a colleague, or before a vacation
handoff.workDetail: a proper handoff, with enough context to carry on without you
handoff.ai: Start a new chat with that context
handoff.aiDetail: the same handoff, pasted in first

onboard.title: 02 · The new teammate
onboard.line: Every new session starts on day one.
onboard.workDetail: nothing carries over unless you say it
onboard.aiDetail: tell it what you would tell a new hire

chunks.title: 03 · Chunks and seams
chunks.line: The seams carry the overall goal.
chunks.work: Break a big project into chunks
chunks.workDetail: define the seams, so each chunk feeds the overall goal
chunks.ai: Split the work into AI tasks
chunks.aiDetail: one task per chunk, the seams as the handover

discipline: Briefing, giving context and checking: the same skill on both sides
closing: More complex projects are now within reach

briefing-context-checking.header: Briefing, context and checking are the discipline
briefing-context-checking.description: Dell'Acqua [1] finds AI helps less experienced people on bounded tasks inside the model's competence; that effective delegation rests on briefing, supplying context and verifying is this project's inference from the research file, not a finding of the study.

dellacqua-jagged-frontier.title: Dell'Acqua et al., Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier, HBS Working Paper 24-013, September 2023 (SSRN 4573321)

new-session-new-contributor.header: A new AI session is a new contributor
new-session-new-contributor.description: Experienced developers described AI as a new contributor lacking tacit knowledge of the repository, which is hard to hand over as context, and spent about 9 percent of their time reviewing and cleaning its output [1].

becker-early-2025-ai.title: Becker, Rush, Barnes, Rein, Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity

experience-predicts-results.header: Experience with the tool predicts results
experience-predicts-results.description: Users with six months or more of tenure show a success rate about 3 to 5 points higher within the same task cluster and delegate less by directive; Anthropic notes learning by doing fits the data but is not proven [1].

anthropic-learning-curves.title: Anthropic, Anthropic Economic Index report: Learning Curves (March 2026)

splitting-tasks-lengthens-them.header: Splitting tasks lengthens what you can finish
splitting-tasks-lengthens-them.description: Users split tasks into steps and pick tasks they expect to work, which accounts for part of the long task lengths seen in practice [1].

anthropic-economic-index-primitives.title: Anthropic, Economic Index: New building blocks for AI use (January 2026)

practise-on-people.title: Practise on people
practise-on-people.script: The good news is that you don't have to wait for a new tool to practise this. You can practise on people, today, at work, so the people skills you already have become your AI skills.

the-handoff.title: The handoff
the-handoff.script: Take the handoff. Next time you hand work to a colleague, before a vacation or any other time, give them a proper handoff with enough context to carry on without you. That is the same move as starting a new chat with the context in it.

the-new-teammate.title: The new teammate
the-new-teammate.script: Or take the new teammate. When you onboard someone, treat it like opening a new AI session: nothing carries over unless you say it, so tell them what you would tell the AI.

chunks-and-seams.title: Chunks and seams
chunks-and-seams.script: Then the big project. When you get a complex one, break it into smaller chunks and define the seams between them, so that each task contributes to the overall goal. Do that, and you can hand the chunks to people or to AI, and stay prolific without losing the thread.

an-invitation.title: An invitation
an-invitation.script: Which brings it back to our coffee question. More complex projects are now within reach, which is not a burden, it is an invitation to grow, so which of these three rows will you start with this week?
